**Executive Briefing Proposal**

Dana Whitfield
General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments

Dear Dana,

**Situation**

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has deployed a customer service chatbot on its support portal. It is piloting AI visual inspection on the German production line and plans AI sales forecasting next year. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded no inventory of AI systems. Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Work toward ISO/IEC 42001 is expected to start next year, though the start date is not fixed.

**What the Briefing Covers for Tamarack Instruments**

The Briefing gives leadership a shared view of the governance priorities ahead of Q2 2027.

* **Regulation.** We will map the EU AI Act and GDPR to the three use cases. This includes how the visual inspection system may be classified and what transparency expectations may apply to the chatbot. These are expectations to verify with counsel, not legal advice. United States requirements are not among your stated drivers, so we will present them only as general landscape items, labeled as such.
* **Readiness.** We will discuss readiness at the piloting stage, starting from the absence of an AI system inventory. The discussion will take account of two stated constraints: customer data must stay in the EU, and the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.
* **Operating model.** We will outline a model using the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). The board-layer reference is AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). We will also consider how the model might align with ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 9001 and the internal audit function named as incumbent frameworks.
* **Principles.** The session is guided by three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.
* **Audience.** The content is designed for the roles named for this audience: General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors.

**Logistics and Price**

* **Format:** Two hours, live virtual.
* **Price:** US$3,000.
* **Session date:** Unknown, to be agreed.

**What You Receive Afterward**

You will receive a written follow-up memo. It summarizes the decisions surfaced, readiness observations and three prioritized recommendations, each mapped to a next program option. The Briefing does not promise certification, audit outcomes or regulatory approval.

**Next Step**

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. Please confirm a preferred session date and the attendee list so we can finalize the tailored agenda.

Kind regards,

AI Governance Academy

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
